Hi Naomi / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked great. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how we could: 1) swap a portion of our reserved throughput to lower-cost feature-only seats, and 2) fold in the new "real-time embedding" add-on without tripping a price-band step-up.

Attached is the current feature matrix you guys saw (WellPath_feature-matrix_v2.xlsx). High level asks from Legal/Finance:
- A transparent step-down path in case usage falls 20% (we need proration mechanics).
- One-off onboarding credit for the embedding add-on pilot (30 days).
- Confirmation that quantized model variants do not void SLA for critical endpoints.

Can you propose a concise swap/rebalance plan with numbers? We are aiming to decide by end of month.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product Partnerships
WellPath Health

Subject: Re: Packaging options — follow up and ask

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the matrix.

Quick summary of what we can do and the follow-up items:
1) Swap / step-down mechanics: we can support a staged downgrade path where up to 25% of reserved throughput converts to "feature seats" (lower-cost SKU) with a 30-day proration window and a one-time conversion fee. If usage drops more than 25% within a quarter, we allow a single prorated adjustment without penalty.

2) Embedding add-on pilot: we can offer a 30-day onboarding credit equivalent to $5k of tokens for initial pilots. After the pilot, the add-on is billed monthly at the add-on unit rate.

3) Quantized variants and SLA: quantized model variants are allowed on customer plans; we guarantee model parity checks and a 99.5% availability SLA for critical endpoints when using Redwood-verified quantized builds. Any regression in quality is covered by our rollback policy.

I'll work with Karthik to put concrete numbers into an amended master amendment (MA). Karthik — can you run two delta scenarios (A: convert 20% throughput to feature seats; B: convert 40% with a staged 2-month grace period) and include monthly cost, per-token delta, and projected 90-day savings?

Lena — want us to include a small canary (10% traffic) on dedicated capacity during the pilot? That would reduce risk for the critical endpoint.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Enterprise Growth
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging options — follow up and ask

Naomi / Kim / Lena — attached I dropped two scenario sheets into the shared Drive link and summarized below. Numbers are rounded.

Scenario A (20% convert to feature seats):
- Current reserved throughput: 1,000 rps equivalent -> convert 200 rps to feature seats
- One-time conversion fee: $3,000
- Monthly cost delta: -$6,200 (WellPath reduces monthly spend due to lower unit rate on feature seats)
- 90-day net: ~$13,600 savings (after conversion fee)
- Impact on SLAs: none (we keep critical endpoint pinned to dedicated capacity)

Scenario B (40% convert to feature seats with 2-month grace):
- Convert 400 rps -> staged over 60 days (200 rps month 1, 200 rps month 2)
- One-time conversion fee: $5,000
- Monthly cost delta: -$12,000 once full; but initial two months savings are smaller due to staged billing
- 90-day net: ~$18,400 savings (after conversion fee)
- Risk: requires stricter traffic routing rules; recommend canary for first 2 weeks

Embedding add-on pilot: credit = $5k for 30 days; projected incremental spend after pilot at full use ~ $1,800/month.

Recommendations:
- If WellPath wants low operational risk, pick Scenario A and take the embedding pilot with a canary on dedicated for 14 days.
- If aggressive cost-first posture, pick Scenario B and accept 2-week canary + staged roll.

I've added the scenario sheets to: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/wellpath-packaging (link above).

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
